title: Lift and transport cocones along coherent diagram and apex equivalences
statement: Use quasicategories, coherent functor simplicial sets, equivalence edges, constant diagrams and colimiting cocones of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], in a universe containing all the data. Let $K$ be any small simplicial set, $\mathcal C$ a quasicategory and $\mathscr D=\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal C)$. Let $d,d':K\to\mathcal C$, $p,p'\in\mathcal C$, and $\sigma:d\to\Delta_Kp$ be a cocone. For every equivalence edge $e:d\to d'$ of $\mathscr D$ and equivalence edge $a:p\to p'$ of $\mathcal C$, there exist a cocone $\sigma':d'\to\Delta_Kp'$ and an equivalence edge $H:\sigma\to\sigma'$ in $\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,\mathscr D)$ whose source-endpoint restriction is exactly $e$ and whose target-endpoint restriction is exactly $\Delta_Ka$. For every such $\sigma'$ and $H$, the cocone $\sigma$ is colimiting if and only if $\sigma'$ is colimiting. This invariance also holds for the images of such a square $H$ under any functor $G:\mathcal C\to\mathcal E$ to a quasicategory: the image of $\sigma$ is colimiting if and only if the image of $\sigma'$ is colimiting. No existence of other colimits and no colimit-preservation assumption on $G$ are imposed; the empty shape $K=\varnothing$ is included.

source.place: Agent lemma isolating the cocone comparison in the dual proof of Proposition 7.5.6, printed p. 373; sections 3.5 and 6.2 for coherent equivalence and colimit conventions. No Stacks tag states this quasicategorical transport result.

proof.text:
By [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus], $\mathscr D=\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal C)$ is a quasicategory. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-isofibration-exponentiation] to the degreewise inclusion $\partial\Delta^1\hookrightarrow\Delta^1$ and the quasicategory $\mathscr D$. Its restriction map is an isofibration
$$r:\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,\mathscr D)\longrightarrow\mathscr D\times\mathscr D.$$
The target identifies degreewise with the two endpoint restrictions. The constant-diagram functor sends the inverse edge and inverse triangles for $a$ to inverse witnesses for $\Delta_Ka$. The edge $(e,\Delta_Ka)$ is an equivalence in the target: equivalently it is a transformation on the discrete two-point shape, whose two components are equivalences, so the pointwise criterion in the cone-calculus node applies. Its source is $r(\sigma)$. The specified-source equivalence-lifting clause of the isofibration node therefore gives an equivalence $H$ starting at $\sigma$, with $r(H)=(e,\Delta_Ka)$ exactly. Its terminal object is an arrow $\sigma':d'\to\Delta_Kp'$, the required cocone.

source.place: Corollary 4.4.5.3 (01F3), applied to the boundary of the interval; pointwise equivalences are Theorem 4.4.4.4 (01DK).

proof.text: Write $c$ for the canonical composition classes of [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition] (in $\mathcal C$, and in $\mathscr D$, which is a quasicategory by step 1); precomposition $v^*=c(-,v)$ and postcomposition $v_*=c(v,-)$ by an edge $v$ are the restrictions of $c$ to the vertex $v$, and depend only on its component class. Let $v:x\to y$ be an equivalence edge with inverse edge $w:y\to x$ and inverse $2$-simplices with boundary triples $(v,w,\mathrm{id}_x)$ and $(w,v,\mathrm{id}_y)$. The $2$-simplex clause of that node gives $[w][v]=[\mathrm{id}_x]$ and $[v][w]=[\mathrm{id}_y]$. For a vertex $z$, the composite $v^*w^*:\operatorname{Map}(x,z)\to\operatorname{Map}(x,z)$ is $f\mapsto c(c(f,w),v)$, the restriction of $c\circ(c\times1)$ to $\operatorname{Map}(x,z)\times\{w\}\times\{v\}$; restricting the associativity homotopy for the vertices $x,y,x,z$ gives $v^*w^*\simeq c(-,c(w,v))$. The vertex $c(w,v)$ lies in the component $[w][v]=[\mathrm{id}_x]$, so by component dependence and unitality $c(-,c(w,v))\simeq c(-,\mathrm{id}_x)\simeq\mathrm{id}$. The same argument gives $w^*v^*\simeq\mathrm{id}$, and, using the other associativity order, $v_*w_*\simeq\mathrm{id}$ and $w_*v_*\simeq\mathrm{id}$. Hence $v^*:\operatorname{Map}(y,z)\to\operatorname{Map}(x,z)$ and $v_*$ are simplicial homotopy equivalences of Kan complexes with homotopy inverses $w^*$, $w_*$. Apply this to $v=a$ in $\mathcal C$ and to $v=e$ in $\mathscr D$. No Hom bifunctor is used.

source.place: Corollary 8.3.5.8 (046J) and Remark 8.3.5.9 (03PD); written out from the associativity, unit and component-dependence clauses of lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition.

proof.text:
Fix any $\sigma'$ and $H$ as in the statement, with $c$ as in step 2. For $z\in\mathcal C$ let $U_{\sigma,z}:\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(p,z)\to\operatorname{Map}_{\mathscr D}(d,\Delta_Kz)$, $u\mapsto c(\Delta_K(u),\sigma)$, be the map of the cocone criterion of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus], and define $U_{\sigma',z}$ similarly; here $\Delta_K$ on mapping spaces is postcomposition of pinched simplices with the simplicial map $\Delta_K:\mathcal C\to\mathscr D$.

(a) Functoriality. Let $F:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ be any simplicial map of quasicategories. Postcomposition with $F$ gives maps $F_M$, $F_U$, $F_V$ of the right-pinched spaces, the arrow spaces $U(-,-)$ and the triangle spaces $V(-,-,-)$ of [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition], and strictly $\theta F_V=(F_U\times F_U)\theta$, $\ell F_V=F_U\ell$. By [lem-coef-infinity-pinch-comparison], $j F_M=F_Uj$. Since the $\theta$ and $j$ are homotopy equivalences of Kan complexes, $[\theta]^{-1}(F_U\times F_U)=[F_V][\theta]^{-1}$, hence
$$[j]\,c\,(F_M\times F_M)=[\ell][\theta]^{-1}([F_Uj]\times[F_Uj])=[F_U][\ell][\theta]^{-1}([j]\times[j])=[F_U][j]c=[j][F_M]c,$$
and cancelling the invertible $[j]$ gives $c(F_M\times F_M)\simeq F_Mc$ as maps of whole mapping spaces. With $F=\Delta_K$ and the second variable restricted to the vertex $a$: $c(\Delta_K(u),\Delta_Ka)\simeq\Delta_K(c(u,a))$ as maps in $u\in\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(p',z)$.

(b) The square. $H:\Delta^1\times\Delta^1\to\mathscr D$ has vertices $d,\Delta_Kp,d',\Delta_Kp'$, edges $\sigma,\sigma',e,\Delta_Ka$ and a diagonal $\delta:d\to\Delta_Kp'$, and its two nondegenerate $2$-simplices have edge triples $(e,\sigma',\delta)$ and $(\sigma,\Delta_Ka,\delta)$. The $2$-simplex clause of [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition] gives $[\sigma'][e]=[\delta]=[\Delta_Ka][\sigma]$, so the vertices $c(\sigma',e)$ and $c(\Delta_Ka,\sigma)$ of $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathscr D}(d,\Delta_Kp')$ lie in one component.

(c) Restricting the associativity homotopies to vertices, using component dependence of precomposition and then (a), one gets homotopies of maps of the whole space $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(p',z)$:
$$e^*U_{\sigma',z}(u)=c(c(\Delta_Ku,\sigma'),e)\simeq c(\Delta_Ku,c(\sigma',e))\simeq c(\Delta_Ku,c(\Delta_Ka,\sigma))\simeq c(c(\Delta_Ku,\Delta_Ka),\sigma)\simeq c(\Delta_K(c(u,a)),\sigma)=U_{\sigma,z}a^*(u).$$
Thus $e^*U_{\sigma',z}\simeq U_{\sigma,z}a^*$, using the actual square $H$, not merely the existence of endpoint equivalences.

source.place: Corollary 8.3.5.8 (046J) and Remark 8.3.5.9 (03PD); the functoriality of composition classes (a) is written out from the characterization in lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition and the naturality of j in lem-coef-infinity-pinch-comparison.

proof.text: The cocone criterion of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus], dualized, says that $\sigma$ (resp. $\sigma'$) is colimiting if and only if $U_{\sigma,z}$ (resp. $U_{\sigma',z}$) is a weak homotopy equivalence for every $z$. By step 2, $a^*$ and $e^*$ are simplicial homotopy equivalences, hence weak homotopy equivalences by [lem-cbc-simplicial-homotopy-equivalence-weak]. Simplicially homotopic maps $f_0,f_1:A\to B$ are weak homotopy equivalences together: if $h:A\times\Delta^1\to B$ is the homotopy, the endpoint inclusions $i_0,i_1:A\to A\times\Delta^1$ have homotopy inverse the projection (the homotopy $A\times\Delta^1\times\Delta^1\to A\times\Delta^1$ induced by $\min:[1]\times[1]\to[1]$), so they are weak equivalences by the same node, and $f_k=hi_k$. Weak homotopy equivalences satisfy two-out-of-three, since bijections and group isomorphisms do. Applied to $e^*U_{\sigma',z}\simeq U_{\sigma,z}a^*$ from step 3: if $U_{\sigma',z}$ is a weak equivalence, so are $e^*U_{\sigma',z}$, $U_{\sigma,z}a^*$ and hence $U_{\sigma,z}$; conversely if $U_{\sigma,z}$ is, so are $U_{\sigma,z}a^*$, $e^*U_{\sigma',z}$ and hence $U_{\sigma',z}$. Taking all $z$, $\sigma$ is colimiting if and only if $\sigma'$ is.

source.place: Agent consequence of the dual cocone criterion and the whole-space homotopy of steps 2–3.

proof.text: For a functor $G:\mathcal C\to\mathcal E$, postcomposition defines a simplicial functor $G_K:\mathscr D\to\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal E)$ by [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. It sends constant diagrams to constant diagrams and sends the displayed square $H$ to a square with endpoint edges $G_Ke$ and $\Delta_KG(a)$. A simplicial map preserves equivalence edges by applying it to inverse triangles, and $G_K\Delta_K=\Delta_KG$ as simplicial maps $\mathcal C\to\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal E)$, so the endpoint edge $G_K(\Delta_Ka)$ is exactly $\Delta_K(Ga)$; steps 2–4 (which need of the square only its two $2$-simplices and of the endpoints only that they are equivalence edges) apply in $\mathcal E$ and give colimitingness of $G\sigma$ if and only if that of $G\sigma'$. No colimit-preservation assumption on $G$ is used. When $K=\varnothing$, the functor simplicial set is the point and the cocone category is $\mathcal C$ by the degreewise definition, so the criterion specializes to invariance of initiality under the given apex equivalence.

source.place: Agent specialization of steps 2–4; degreewise postcomposition and the empty-shape pullback are the definitions in the cited node.
